'''Vincent E. Courtillot''' ({{IPA|fr|vɛ̃sɑ̃ kuʁtijo|lang}}; born 6 March 1948) is an emeritus French [[geophysics|geophysicist]], prominent among the researchers who are critical of the hypothesis that [[impact events]] are a primary cause of [[mass extinction]] of life forms on the Earth. He is known for his book ''La Vie en catastrophes'' (Paris, [[Fayard]], 1995), translated into English as ''Evolutionary catastrophes'' (1999).

== Biography ==
Courtillot is an engineer from the [[École nationale supérieure des Mines de Paris]]. He then studied at [[Stanford University]].<ref>In 1972, he wrote there a report ''[http://searchworks.stanford.edu/view/1967107 Inverse filtering of marine magnetic anomalies]''</ref> In 1974, he was awarded a doctorate by [[Pierre and Marie Curie University|University Paris 6]]<ref>''[http://www.worldcat.org/oclc/490570807 Quelques applications du problème inverse à l'étude des anomalies magnétiques, gravimétriques et géothermiques]'', thèse de troisième cycle, Université Paris-6</ref> and in 1977 a state doctorate by [[Paris Diderot University|University Paris 7]].<ref>''Sur l'analyse de certaines variations spatiales et temporelles du champ magnétique terrestre'', thèse de doctorat d'État, Université Paris-7.</ref>

He has pursued an academic career in France and the United States, including teaching stints at [[Caltech]] and the [[University of Minnesota]], and work with the [[IPGP|Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris]] (where he has been director since 2004), and the Ministry of National Education in France. (From 1998 to 2001 Courtillot served under [[Claude Allègre]] as director of research when Allègre was [[Minister of National Education (France)|Minister for National Education, Research and Technology]].) Courtillot is currently Professor of Geophysics at the [[Paris Diderot University]]. He has published in excess of 150 papers in scientific journals, with some emphasis on the specialty of [[paleomagnetism]]; he has served as editorial advisor to the French journal ''[[La Recherche (magazine)|La Recherche]].''

Vincent Courtillot was elected to membership in the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in November 2003. He is also a member of the ''Fondation Ecologie d'Avenir'' since 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fondationecologiedavenir.org/Conseil_Orientation.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006034618/http://www.fondationecologiedavenir.org/Conseil_Orientation.htm|archive-date=2011-10-06|title=Fondation Ecologie d'Avenir: Le Conseil d'Orientation}}</ref>

== Research ==
{{BLP unsourced section|date=August 2022}}
Courtillot favors the hypothesis that major [[mass extinctions]] are caused by massive episodes of vulcanism: that the [[Permian-Triassic extinction event|Permian-Triassic (P/T) extinction]] that ended the [[Paleozoic Era]] was caused by the [[Siberian Traps]] eruption, and the [[Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event]] that ended the [[Mesozoic Era]] was caused by the [[Deccan Traps]] [[Volcanism|vulcanism]] in India. His position is generally in opposition to the hypothesis famously championed by [[Luis Walter Alvarez|Luis Alvarez]] and [[Walter Alvarez]], that the K/T extinction that saw the end of the non-avian [[dinosaur]]s was primarily due to the [[asteroid]] impact at [[Chicxulub crater|Chicxulub]] on the [[Yucatan Peninsula]]. However, Courtillot does not dispute the scientifically-determined facts of the [[Chicxulub crater|Chicxulub impact]]; rather, he argues that the totality of the available evidence supports a thesis that [[mass extinctions]] are generally caused by volcanic action.

== Magnetic field and climate ==
He is currently at the centre of a scientific controversy<ref name="BardDelaygue2008">{{cite journal | last1=Bard | first1=Edouard | last2=Delaygue | first2=Gilles | year=2008 | title=Comment on "Are there connections between the Earth's magnetic field and climate?" by V. Courtillot, Y. Gallet, J.-L. Le Mouël, F. Fluteau, A. Genevey EPSL 253, 328, 2007 | journal=Earth and Planetary Science Letters | volume=265 | issue=1–2 | pages=302–307 | doi=10.1016/j.epsl.2007.09.046| bibcode=2008E&PSL.265..302B }}</ref> regarding the publication of one of his papers in the journal ''[[Earth and Planetary Science Letters]] (EPSL)'' entitled "Are there connections between the Earth's magnetic field and climate?" by V. Courtillot, Y. Gallet, J.-L. Le Mouël, F. Fluteau, A. Genevey (2007) EPSL 253, 328. There have been articles in ''[[Le Monde]]'' on 15 January 2008,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.lemonde.fr/planete/article/2008/01/15/point-de-vue-de-vincent-courtillot_999585_3244.html|title=Point de vue de Vincent Courtillot|date=15 January 2008|via=Le Monde|newspaper=Le Monde.fr}}</ref> and in ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' on 11 January 2008<ref name="Pasotti2008">{{cite journal|last1=Pasotti|first1=Jacopo|date=11 January 2008|title=Daggers are drawn over revived cosmic ray-climate link |journal=Science|volume=319|issue=5860|page=144|doi=10.1126/science.319.5860.144|pmid=18187627|s2cid=8438851|doi-access=free}}</ref> concerning the debate over this paper.

He is usually considered<ref name="BardDelaygue2008" /> to be a [[global warming denier]], often associated with [[Claude Allègre]]. Vincent Courtillot asserted that his collaboration with oil companies [[Total S.A.|Total]] and [[Schlumberger]] on {{CO2}} sequestration ([[Carbon capture and storage|CCS]])<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.france-info.com/chroniques-parlons-net-2009-11-27-parlons-net-vincent-courtillot-un-climatosceptique-tempere-373798-81-264.html | title=Franceinfo - Actualités en temps réel et info en direct}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ipgp.fr/pages/020203.php |title=Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris - Stockage géologique du CO<sub>2</sub> |website=www.ipgp.fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090618214603/http://www.ipgp.fr/pages/020203.php |archive-date=2009-06-18}}</ref> has no influence on his research and results.
